aim: Audit the 34 canonical Sexual Ethics debates not included in the prior 21-debate Catholic atomic-claim batches, focusing on opponent's actual authorship and full-text versus contextual/mediated/illustrative source status. Source routing is checked for 102 opposition/appeal/counter stages; a linked URL alone does not constitute verified author attribution or whole-argument proof.

cases.original_section_locator: chapter IV, paragraphs 1–5
cases.scope_limitation: Mill On Liberty Chapter IV: distinguishes liberty from state/social compulsion and explicitly allows persuasion, education and disapproval in specified forms; it does not claim every private act good.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: A familiar liberty-based objection holds that adults should not face state coercion for private sexual choices that do not harm others. John Stuart Mill argues particularly against coercive social authority; a further argument is needed to claim that every unharming choice is morally good.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Une objection courante fondée sur la liberté soutient que les adultes ne devraient pas subir de contrainte étatique pour des choix sexuels privés qui ne nuisent pas à autrui. John Stuart Mill conteste surtout l’autorité sociale coercitive ; il faut un argument supplémentaire pour conclure que tout choix sans dommage est moralement bon.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: This is attractive because it protects liberty and correctly treats unjust harm as morally serious. It also guards against intrusive rules based only on disgust or convention.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Cette position séduit parce qu’elle protège la liberté et reconnaît à juste titre que le tort injuste est moralement grave. Elle protège aussi contre des règles intrusives fondées seulement sur le dégoût ou la convention.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Mill himself allows persuasion and moral education without coercion. But why should a non-Catholic accept the specifically Catholic account of sexuality?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mill lui-même admet la persuasion et l’éducation morale sans coercition. Mais pourquoi un non-catholique accepterait-il la conception spécifiquement catholique de la sexualité ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: No original author passage verified for this exact constructed question
cases.scope_limitation: Scripture-silence challenge is editorially constructed; Curran CDF 1986 record is historical church response and not the author's verbatim objection.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The Gospels do not name contraception, IVF or many modern practices. If Christ did not discuss a technique expressly, why should Christians accept a later moral judgment about it?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les Évangiles ne nomment ni la contraception, ni la FIV, ni bien des pratiques modernes. Si le Christ n’a pas évoqué expressément une technique, pourquoi les chrétiens devraient-ils accepter un jugement moral ultérieur ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Later Christian formulations should not be presented as though Jesus had spoken those exact words in the Gospels.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les formulations chrétiennes ultérieures ne doivent pas être présentées comme si Jésus avait prononcé exactement ces mots dans les Évangiles.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But how do we know later Christians are applying Jesus rather than importing their own prejudices?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais comment savoir si les chrétiens ultérieurs appliquent Jésus plutôt qu’ils n’importent leurs propres préjugés ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Charles Curran 1987, sexuality/natural-law methodology, paragraphs 2–10
cases.scope_limitation: Curran's 1987 article genuinely questions inherited physicalist premises; this objection about Paul and local custom is not documented as an exact Curran quotation.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Paul was an ancient man shaped by Jewish and Greco-Roman assumptions. His sexual prohibitions may reflect his culture rather than permanent moral truth.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Paul était un homme de l’Antiquité façonné par des présupposés juifs et gréco-romains. Ses interdictions sexuelles peuvent refléter sa culture plutôt qu’une vérité morale permanente.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Historical context matters, and Christians can misread ancient texts when they ignore language, genre and social assumptions.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le contexte historique compte, et les chrétiens peuvent mal lire les textes anciens lorsqu’ils ignorent la langue, le genre et les présupposés sociaux.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But even theological reasoning can be shaped by mistaken ancient anthropology.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais même un raisonnement théologique peut être façonné par une anthropologie antique erronée.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Charles Curran 1987, paragraphs on authoritative noninfallible hierarchical teaching and loyal opposition
cases.scope_limitation: Curran argues non-infallible hierarchical moral teaching may be mistaken and makes a case for loyal dissent; do not ascribe to him a blanket dismissal of all moral norms.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: In his 1987 essay, Charles Curran argues that authoritative non-infallible moral judgments carry weight but may contain error. He cites doctrinal developments, different degrees of authority, and the possibility of loyal dissent in specific cases. If the Church can correct a non-definitive judgment, how can permanent moral doctrine be distinguished from reformable applications?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dans son article de 1987, Charles Curran soutient que les jugements moraux non infaillibles faisant autorité possèdent une force réelle, mais peuvent être erronés. Il invoque les développements doctrinaux, les degrés d'autorité et la possibilité d'un dissentiment loyal dans des cas précis. Si l'Église peut corriger un jugement non définitif, comment distinguer la doctrine morale permanente d'une application réformable ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Curran distinguishes definitive teaching from authoritative non-infallible judgments, and genuine historical developments require explanation. Different levels of teaching authority cannot simply be collapsed into one undifferentiated claim of infallibility.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Curran distingue l’enseignement définitif des jugements non infaillibles qui font néanmoins autorité, et les développements historiques réels demandent une explication. Les différents degrés d’autorité doctrinale ne peuvent être confondus en une seule prétention indifférenciée à l’infaillibilité.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But isn’t that just selecting examples that support continuity and ignoring difficult cases?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais cela ne revient-il pas à choisir des exemples favorables à la continuité et à ignorer les cas difficiles ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Freud 1908 text not independently accessible this pass
cases.scope_limitation: The Freud edition server returned an error; 1908 argument is presented as historical theory, not established modern psychiatric causation.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: In his 1908 essay on civilized sexual morality and modern nervousness, Freud argues that cultural restraints can contribute to psychological distress and that people's capacity for sexual sublimation differs. If severe restraint harms some individuals, why should chastity always be treated as a virtue rather than a potential burden?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dans son essai de 1908 sur la morale sexuelle civilisée et la nervosité moderne, Freud soutient que certaines restrictions sociales peuvent contribuer à la souffrance psychique et que la capacité de sublimation varie selon les personnes. Si une retenue excessive nuit à certains, pourquoi la chasteté serait-elle toujours une vertu plutôt qu'une charge potentielle ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The criticism has force when chastity is taught as shame, disgust toward the body or constant anxiety about temptation.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La critique est forte lorsque la chasteté est enseignée comme honte, dégoût du corps ou anxiété constante devant la tentation.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But suppression of desire can still cause psychological harm.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais la suppression du désir peut tout de même causer un dommage psychologique.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Study original methods and sample pending
cases.scope_limitation: Specific 2016 priest wellbeing study not re-read; do not infer all forms of celibacy psychologically harmful or all healthy.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: A qualitative study of 15 US priests documented both benefits and psychological difficulties associated with celibacy and obedience. Can lifelong celibacy involve distress or isolation that defenders should take seriously?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Une étude qualitative auprès de quinze prêtres américains a relevé des effets bénéfiques comme des difficultés psychologiques liés au célibat et à l'obéissance. Le célibat perpétuel peut-il entraîner des souffrances ou un isolement qu'il faut prendre au sérieux ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Celibacy can indeed be lived badly, and human beings genuinely need intimacy, friendship and belonging.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le célibat peut réellement être mal vécu, et l’être humain a véritablement besoin d’intimité, d’amitié et d’appartenance.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But even if possible, why call it a higher vocation?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais même si c’est possible, pourquoi l’appeler une vocation supérieure ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Pew 2019 Why people get married or move in, paragraphs on cohabiter major factors and seriousness
cases.scope_limitation: Pew reports 38% financial and 37% convenience major motives among cohabiters; 23% instead refers to people neither engaged nor in a very serious relationship. Survey measures reported reasons, not outcomes or motives to test compatibility.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Pew's 2019 US survey found that 38% of cohabiters cited finances and 37% cited convenience as major reasons for moving in together. That survey described reported motives, not whether cohabitation improves marriage outcomes. Can the desire to understand daily compatibility justify cohabitation before marriage?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Selon l'enquête américaine Pew de 2019, 38 % des personnes en cohabitation invoquaient les finances et 37 % la commodité comme raisons majeures d'emménager ensemble. L'enquête rapporte des motifs déclarés, sans démontrer que la cohabitation améliore les mariages ultérieurs. Le désir de connaître sa compatibilité quotidienne justifie-t-il la vie commune avant le mariage ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Learning compatibility is genuinely important, and the Pew survey describes people's motives. It does not demonstrate that cohabitation causes better marital outcomes.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Connaître sa compatibilité est réellement important ; l'enquête Pew décrit les motifs déclarés, mais ne démontre pas que la cohabitation améliore causalement le devenir d'un mariage.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But many married couples discover incompatibilities only after living together. Isn’t cohabitation simply prudent risk reduction?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais beaucoup de couples découvrent des incompatibilités seulement après avoir vécu ensemble. La cohabitation n’est-elle pas simplement une réduction prudente du risque ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Illustrative / institutional landing page, not original philosophical argument
cases.scope_limitation: Representative challenge about deliberate looking is not a first-person Planned Parenthood argument; original page not re-read.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Looking is not touching. If someone attractive passes by, enjoying the sight seems harmless and private, especially if there is no intention to approach or cheat.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Regarder n’est pas toucher. Si une personne attirante passe, apprécier ce qu’on voit paraît inoffensif et privé, surtout s’il n’y a aucune intention de l’aborder ou de tromper son partenaire.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: An involuntary attraction or first glance is different from a chosen sexual act. Human beings notice beauty and attractiveness without deciding to do so.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Une attirance involontaire ou un premier regard diffère d’un acte sexuel choisi. L’être humain remarque la beauté et l’attirance sans l’avoir décidé.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But if an attractive person is deliberately dressed to attract attention, isn’t the viewer simply responding to what is offered?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais si une personne s’habille délibérément pour attirer l’attention, le spectateur ne fait-il pas que répondre à ce qui lui est présenté ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: General institutional context only
cases.scope_limitation: Relationship courtesy and exclusivity challenge is composed rather than quoted; Planned Parenthood general relationship page not verified as stating the same view.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Flirting is just social play. Unless someone actually cheats, joking, teasing or enjoying attention from another person should not be treated as infidelity.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le flirt n’est qu’un jeu social. Tant qu’il n’y a pas tromperie réelle, plaisanter, taquiner ou apprécier l’attention d’une autre personne ne devrait pas être traité comme une infidélité.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Much ordinary friendliness is ambiguous, and moralizing every smile or playful remark would be both unrealistic and scrupulous.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Beaucoup de comportements amicaux ordinaires sont ambigus, et moraliser chaque sourire ou plaisanterie serait irréaliste et scrupuleux.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Does that make harmless attraction to someone else disloyal?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Cela rend-il déloyale toute attirance innocente pour quelqu’un d’autre ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: General sex education context only
cases.scope_limitation: Sex acts below intercourse objection is editorially constructed; Planned Parenthood health information is not a theological treatise.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If engaged partners avoid intercourse and pregnancy, why should other deliberately genital sexual acts still be contrary to chastity? Their intention may be affection rather than rejection of marriage.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si des fiancés évitent le rapport conjugal et la grossesse, pourquoi les autres actes génitaux délibérés resteraient-ils contraires à la chasteté ? Leur intention peut être l'affection et non le rejet du mariage.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Intercourse and other sexual acts differ in physical structure and consequences; not every act carries the same pregnancy risk.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L’union sexuelle et les autres actes sexuels diffèrent par leur structure physique et leurs conséquences ; tous ne comportent pas le même risque de grossesse.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: What about sleeping in the same bed, nudity or heavy making-out if the couple honestly intends not to orgasm?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Qu’en est-il de dormir dans le même lit, d’être nus ensemble ou de s’embrasser intensément si le couple veut sincèrement éviter l’orgasme ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: CDF 2012 Notification homosexual unions / Just Love p.293; Farley 4 June 2012 own response
cases.scope_limitation: Farley's gay marriage recognition passage quoted as p.293 by CDF; her June 2012 first-person response affirms justice framework and objects to being represented only by selective extracts. Complete book not accessed.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Margaret Farley argues that legal recognition of same-sex partnerships and marriages can counter social rejection (Just Love, p.293, quoted in the CDF's 2012 Notification). Her position raises a substantive challenge: if two people of the same sex can show love, fidelity and commitment, why should civil and ecclesial understandings of marriage differ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Margaret Farley soutient que la reconnaissance juridique des unions et mariages de même sexe peut contribuer à combattre le rejet social (Just Love, p.293, cité dans la Notification de la CDF de 2012). Son argument pose une difficulté réelle : si deux personnes du même sexe peuvent manifester amour, fidélité et engagement, pourquoi les conceptions civile et ecclésiale du mariage devraient-elles différer ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Affection, loyalty, sacrifice and stable commitment are genuine relational goods.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L’affection, la loyauté, le sacrifice et l’engagement stable sont de véritables biens relationnels.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But many heterosexual marriages never have children.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais beaucoup de mariages hétérosexuels n’ont jamais d’enfants.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Archived source, page context uncollated
cases.scope_limitation: Archived scenario about consensual sexual acts; institutional safer-sex article is not an author of the specific moral claim.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Once a couple is married, oral stimulation, manual stimulation and sex toys are simply different ways of pleasuring one’s spouse. If both consent, prohibiting them seems like unnecessary micromanagement of the marriage bed.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Une fois marié, la stimulation orale, la stimulation manuelle et les jouets sexuels ne sont que différentes manières de donner du plaisir à son conjoint. Si les deux consentent, les interdire paraît être une intrusion inutile dans le lit conjugal.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Marriage genuinely gives spouses a broad sphere of legitimate sexual intimacy, and Catholic teaching does not provide a catalogue of forbidden body parts or techniques.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le mariage donne réellement aux époux un large espace d’intimité sexuelle légitime, et l’enseignement catholique ne fournit pas un catalogue de parties du corps ou de techniques interdites.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Isn’t that still a technical obsession with where orgasm occurs rather than with marital love?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Cela ne reste-t-il pas une obsession technique sur le lieu de l’orgasme plutôt que sur l’amour conjugal ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Archived third-party organisational materials not verified in full
cases.scope_limitation: Archived nonmonogamy debate uses organisational descriptive context; not an attributed direct author quote.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If both spouses agree to non-monogamy, adultery should no longer apply because no one is being deceived. Fidelity can be defined by the couple however they choose.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si les deux époux acceptent la non-monogamie, l’adultère ne devrait plus s’appliquer puisqu’il n’y a aucune tromperie. Le couple peut définir la fidélité comme il l’entend.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Secrecy and betrayal add serious wrongs to adultery, and consensual non-monogamy removes some of those additional wrongs.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le secret et la trahison ajoutent des maux graves à l’adultère, et la non-monogamie consensuelle supprime certains de ces maux supplémentaires.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But why can’t adults redefine their own covenant by mutual agreement?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Pourquoi des adultes ne pourraient-ils pas redéfinir leur propre alliance d’un commun accord ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Archived clinical context unverified
cases.scope_limitation: Archived anal-sex case is editorial challenge; medical risks are not an opponent's written moral thesis.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If spouses are married and mutually consent, anal sex should be no different from other forms of sexual experimentation. The relationship, not anatomy, should determine morality.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si des époux sont mariés et consentent mutuellement, le sexe anal ne devrait pas être différent d’autres formes d’expérimentation sexuelle. La relation, non l’anatomie, devrait déterminer la morale.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: No body part is intrinsically dirty or shameful; moral theology judges the human act and its object, not anatomy in isolation.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Aucune partie du corps n’est intrinsèquement sale ou honteuse ; la théologie morale juge l’acte humain et son objet, non l’anatomie prise isolément.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Isn’t saying “disputed” just avoiding a clear answer?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dire « disputé » n’est-ce pas simplement éviter une réponse claire ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: CDF 2012 Notification masturbation / Just Love p.236; Farley 2012 response
cases.scope_limitation: CDF cites Farley's masturbation paragraph from Just Love p.236 and author independently describes her justice-oriented methodological framework in 2012. The entire book and surrounding p.236 arguments remain inaccessible.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Margaret Farley holds that the justice of masturbation should be judged largely by its effects on a person's wellbeing and freedom rather than by an intrinsic moral prohibition (Just Love, p.236, quoted in the CDF's 2012 Notification). If no one else is harmed, why should the act itself be considered gravely disordered?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Margaret Farley estime que la justice morale de la masturbation doit être appréciée surtout selon ses effets sur le bien-être et la liberté de la personne plutôt qu'en vertu d'une interdiction intrinsèque (Just Love, p.236, cité dans la Notification de la CDF de 2012). Si personne d'autre n'en subit de préjudice, pourquoi l'acte lui-même serait-il jugé gravement désordonné ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Masturbation lacks some additional wrongs found in adultery, coercion or exploitation.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La masturbation ne comporte pas certains maux supplémentaires de l’adultère, de la contrainte ou de l’exploitation.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Why must sexual pleasure always be integrated into marriage? Pleasure in eating is not limited to a particular relationship, so why should sexuality differ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Pourquoi le plaisir sexuel devrait-il toujours s'inscrire dans le mariage ? Le plaisir de manger n'est pas réservé à une relation particulière ; pourquoi la sexualité serait-elle différente ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Full original Planned Parenthood page not collated
cases.scope_limitation: A consensual pornography challenge is editorial; Planned Parenthood teaching is not a documented argument that consent renders all use morally good.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If adults freely consent to produce and view pornography, and coercion and harmful depictions are guarded against, why should the activity itself be wrong? Could the concern be exploitation and degrading use rather than every erotic depiction?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si des adultes consentent librement à produire et regarder de la pornographie, et que la contrainte ainsi que les représentations nuisibles sont combattues, pourquoi l’activité elle-même serait-elle mauvaise ? Le problème ne serait-il pas plutôt l’exploitation et l’usage dégradant que toute représentation érotique ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Respect for consent and freedom from exploitation are genuine moral concerns. They matter when analyzing pornography, but neither consent nor an unverified assumption about production conditions decides the objective Catholic moral question by itself.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le respect du consentement et l'absence d'exploitation sont de véritables exigences morales. Elles comptent dans l'analyse de la pornographie, mais ni le consentement ni des suppositions non vérifiées sur les conditions de production ne résolvent à eux seuls la question morale objective en doctrine catholique.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: What if the performers themselves enjoy exhibition and feel no degradation?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Et si les interprètes aiment eux-mêmes s’exhiber et ne se sentent pas dégradés ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Privacy and technology premises require independent studies
cases.scope_limitation: Private married recording question is a constructed practical problem, not direct Planned Parenthood advocacy.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The Catechism §2354 defines pornography by displaying real or simulated sexual acts to third parties. Private material created exclusively by spouses poses a different question: does recording intimacy remain prudent and respectful if it is never shared?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le Catéchisme (§2354) définit la pornographie par l'exposition à des tiers d'actes sexuels réels ou simulés. Du matériel créé exclusivement par les époux pose une autre question : enregistrer leur intimité demeure-t-il prudent et respectueux sans aucune diffusion ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The case is genuinely different from third-party pornography because no outside performer is being consumed and the sexual relationship itself is legitimate.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le cas est réellement différent de la pornographie impliquant des tiers parce qu’aucun interprète extérieur n’est consommé et que la relation sexuelle elle-même est légitime.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If both spouses understand the risks and still consent, why should prudence become a moral issue?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si les deux époux comprennent les risques et consentent quand même, pourquoi la prudence deviendrait-elle une question morale ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: CDF 2012 Notification homosexual acts / Just Love p.295; Farley 2012 response
cases.scope_limitation: CDF quotes Farley Just Love p.295 on same-sex ethics; her 2012 firsthand reply explains central justice/relationship ethics. Full book argument is not examined.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Margaret Farley argues that same-sex relationships and sexual activity may be evaluated by the same relational criteria as heterosexual ones (Just Love, p. 295, quoted in the CDF's 2012 Notification). If mutual love, fidelity and justice matter, why exclude a faithful same-sex couple?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Margaret Farley soutient que les relations et actes sexuels entre personnes de même sexe peuvent être jugés selon les mêmes critères relationnels que les autres (Just Love, p. 295, cité dans la Notification de la CDF de 2012). Si amour, fidélité et justice comptent, pourquoi exclure un couple fidèle de même sexe ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Affection, loyalty, sacrifice and other relational goods can be genuinely present and should not be denied or mocked.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L’affection, la loyauté, le sacrifice et d’autres biens relationnels peuvent être réellement présents et ne doivent être ni niés ni ridiculisés.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Isn’t that just privileging biology over love?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Cela ne revient-il pas à privilégier la biologie sur l’amour ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: CDF Farley excerpts are context, not exact authored comparison
cases.scope_limitation: The infertile heterosexual marriage comparison is constructed; Farley's excerpts do not independently substantiate this specific challenge. Avoid describing it as her quotation.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Infertile heterosexual spouses can marry although they cannot conceive. If successful procreation is not required for marriage, why must the man–woman distinction remain essential to its definition?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Des époux hétérosexuels stériles peuvent se marier alors qu'ils ne peuvent concevoir. Si une procréation effective n'est pas requise, pourquoi la différence homme–femme demeure-t-elle essentielle à la définition du mariage ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Actual conception is not required for every marriage or every conjugal act.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La conception effective n’est pas requise pour chaque mariage ni pour chaque acte conjugal.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But why should “type of act” matter if the result is known to be impossible?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Pourquoi le « type d’acte » devrait-il compter si l’on sait que le résultat est impossible ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA 2008 sexual-orientation FAQ: discrimination section
cases.scope_limitation: APA 2008 original explanatory page discusses stereotypes, stigma and prejudice; separate APA policy text not independently read. No causal effect size or clinical prevalence is certified.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The American Psychological Association condemns stigma, discrimination and violence against sexual minorities and reports that such prejudice can harm mental health. If religious language is used to stigmatize gay people, is the Church sufficiently confronting the consequences of that language?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L'American Psychological Association condamne la stigmatisation, la discrimination et les violences contre les minorités sexuelles et relève leurs conséquences possibles sur la santé psychique. Si un langage religieux sert à stigmatiser des personnes homosexuelles, l'Église en affronte-t-elle suffisamment les conséquences ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The concern is serious because moral language can be weaponized, and people have suffered contempt, rejection and violence under religious pretexts.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La préoccupation est sérieuse parce que le langage moral peut être utilisé comme arme, et des personnes ont subi mépris, rejet et violence sous des prétextes religieux.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But in practice the distinction often feels hollow when the teaching denies recognition to a person’s relationship.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais en pratique la distinction paraît souvent vide lorsque l’enseignement refuse de reconnaître la relation d’une personne.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA 2008 sexual-orientation FAQ, mental health / sexual orientation sections
cases.scope_limitation: APA explanatory FAQ states homosexuality is not a mental disorder; objections concern evidence-based psychiatric labeling, not endorsement of any specific Catholic moral norm. The separately cited policy is uncollated.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The American Psychological Association explicitly says same-sex orientation is not a mental disorder and opposes efforts that promise to change orientation. Does a traditional moral account need to change if it once depended on assumptions that homosexuality is a psychiatric disease or that orientation is freely chosen?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L'American Psychological Association affirme expressément que l'orientation homosexuelle n'est pas un trouble mental et rejette les interventions promettant de la modifier. Une morale traditionnelle doit-elle être révisée si elle s'appuyait sur la maladie psychiatrique ou sur le choix volontaire de cette orientation ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Scientific corrections matter. A moral argument that depends on false claims about pathology or voluntariness must be revised.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les corrections scientifiques comptent. Un argument moral fondé sur de fausses affirmations concernant la pathologie ou le caractère volontaire doit être révisé.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But if psychology shows same-sex orientation is stable and unchosen, doesn’t requiring celibacy become unreasonable?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais si la psychologie montre qu’une orientation homosexuelle est stable et non choisie, exiger la continence ne devient-il pas déraisonnable ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: CDF 2012 Notification homosexual unions p.293; Farley original response 2012
cases.scope_limitation: Farley's p.293 CDF quotation specifically advocates legal recognition; her 2012 reply identifies its justice premises and complains of selective representation. Neither text independently proves every civil-law effect.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Margaret Farley argued that legal recognition of civil unions and same-sex marriage could help combat stigma and provide comparable social recognition (Just Love, p. 293, quoted in the CDF's 2012 Notification). Why should a civil state with citizens of different religions reject that equal-recognition case?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Margaret Farley défendait la reconnaissance juridique des unions civiles et du mariage entre personnes de même sexe pour lutter contre la stigmatisation et favoriser une reconnaissance sociale comparable (Just Love, p. 293, cité dans la Notification de la CDF de 2012). Pourquoi un État composé de citoyens de religions diverses devrait-il écarter cet argument d'égalité ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Private religious rules and the coercive power of civil law are distinct; legal restrictions require reasons appropriate to the common good and public justice.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les règles religieuses privées et le pouvoir coercitif de la loi civile sont distincts ; les restrictions juridiques exigent des raisons propres au bien commun et à la justice publique.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But the state already recognizes infertile and childless marriages, so procreation cannot be the public purpose.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais l’État reconnaît déjà les mariages stériles et sans enfants ; la procréation ne peut donc être le but public.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA original institutional page retained but not independently rechecked
cases.scope_limitation: APA gender identity explanatory page not re-read during this source pass; no claim that every sociocultural role is a biological law.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The APA distinguishes biological sex from culturally variable gender roles and recognizes atypical development of sex characteristics. If these concepts differ, which parts of the traditional account describe bodily reality and which merely describe social expectations?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L'APA distingue le sexe biologique des rôles de genre variables selon les cultures et reconnaît des développements atypiques des caractères sexuels. Si ces notions diffèrent, qu'est-ce qui, dans la tradition, décrit le corps et qu'est-ce qui n'est qu'attente sociale ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Many expectations attached to men and women are cultural rather than biologically necessary.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: De nombreuses attentes attachées aux hommes et aux femmes sont culturelles plutôt que biologiquement nécessaires.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But biology itself contains atypical development and ambiguity.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais la biologie elle-même comporte des développements atypiques et des ambiguïtés.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA 2024 policy statement summary lines 21–30
cases.scope_limitation: APA February 2024 policy summary advocates unobstructed access and inclusive care; it is professional association policy rather than an intervention-specific comparative trial. Complete linked PDF not independently visually collated.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The American Psychological Association's February 2024 policy supports access to affirming, evidence-based healthcare for transgender and gender-diverse people and challenges stigmatizing misinformation. How should this clinical-policy position be weighed against Catholic anthropology of the sexed body?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La politique de l'American Psychological Association de février 2024 soutient l'accès à des soins affirmatifs fondés sur les données probantes pour les personnes transgenres et de diverses identités de genre, et critique la désinformation stigmatisante. Comment apprécier cette politique clinique à la lumière de l'anthropologie catholique du corps sexué ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The suffering is real and should never be dismissed as mere ideology. Clinical outcomes matter.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La souffrance est réelle et ne doit jamais être rejetée comme simple idéologie. Les résultats cliniques comptent.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But if an intervention demonstrably reduces suffering, why should anthropology override clinical benefit?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais si une intervention réduit manifestement la souffrance, pourquoi l’anthropologie devrait-elle l’emporter sur le bénéfice clinique ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA 2024 policy summary and scope
cases.scope_limitation: APA 2024 policy discusses stigma and access, not an empirical experiment establishing that any particular form of address causes a quantified mental-health outcome. Full PDF still uncollated.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The American Psychological Association's 2024 policy links gender-related rejection and discrimination to psychological harm and calls for respectful, individualized care. In ordinary conversation, could refusing a person's requested form of address deepen distress even when the speaker disputes the underlying view of gender identity?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La politique de l'American Psychological Association de 2024 relie rejet et discrimination liés au genre à des dommages psychologiques et demande des soins respectueux et individualisés. Dans la conversation ordinaire, refuser la manière dont une personne demande à être appelée pourrait-il accroître sa souffrance, même si l'on conteste sa conception de l'identité de genre ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Language can wound, and gratuitous confrontation or humiliation is contrary to charity.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le langage peut blesser, et la confrontation gratuite ou l’humiliation sont contraires à la charité.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But refusing affirmation may have foreseeable psychological costs.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais refuser l’affirmation peut avoir des coûts psychologiques prévisibles.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: WPATH SOC8 Ch.2 Global Applicability Statements 2.1–2.2; adult and adolescent assessment sections
cases.scope_limitation: WPATH SOC8 is an authored multidisciplinary clinical standards document, with explicit medical necessity, individualized and regional applicability statements; cannot infer efficacy of every procedure without condition-specific studies.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: WPATH's Standards of Care 8 recommends individualized assessment, informed decision-making and clinical options intended to relieve persistent gender-related distress. Where a patient reports serious suffering and potential treatment benefits, what evidence and moral reasons justify withholding a particular intervention?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les Standards of Care 8 de WPATH recommandent une évaluation individualisée, une décision éclairée et des traitements destinés à soulager une souffrance persistante liée au genre. Lorsqu'un patient éprouve une détresse grave et qu'un traitement pourrait lui apporter un bénéfice, quelles preuves et quelles raisons morales justifient le refus de cette intervention ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Adult autonomy is important, and not every medical intervention must restore a diseased organ in a narrow sense.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L’autonomie adulte est importante, et toute intervention médicale ne doit pas nécessairement restaurer un organe malade au sens étroit.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Why privilege the original body if changing it produces a more livable life?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Pourquoi privilégier le corps d’origine si le modifier produit une vie plus vivable ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Singer/Kuhse book chapter preview and ACOG policy not fully collated
cases.scope_limitation: Embryonic moral status and cognitive criteria are constructed illustrative reasoning. The linked ACOG policy and Singer chapter do not establish a single verbatim opponent position.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: In the earliest weeks there is no consciousness, pain, viability or developed brain. Calling an embryo morally equivalent to a born child seems to ignore enormous developmental differences.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dans les premières semaines il n’y a ni conscience, ni douleur, ni viabilité, ni cerveau développé. Traiter moralement un embryon comme un enfant né semble ignorer d’énormes différences de développement.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The developmental differences are real. An early embryo does not presently exercise the capacities of a fetus near birth, much less an adult.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les différences de développement sont réelles. Un embryon précoce n’exerce pas actuellement les capacités d’un fœtus proche de la naissance, encore moins celles d’un adulte.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: What about a fetus with a grave anomaly and little prospect of surviving after birth?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Qu’en est-il d’un fœtus atteint d’une grave anomalie et ayant peu de chances de survivre après la naissance ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: ACOG source only referenced without exact matched original passage
cases.scope_limitation: Rape-pregnancy dilemma is an illustrative moral challenge, not exact language ascribed to ACOG; maternal trauma outcomes require specialist original data.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Pregnancy caused by rape can force a woman to carry the physical consequences of a violent crime for months. Requiring that pregnancy to continue can seem like making the victim sacrifice herself for a child she never chose to conceive.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Une grossesse issue d’un viol peut obliger une femme à porter pendant des mois les conséquences physiques d’un crime violent. Exiger la poursuite de cette grossesse peut sembler demander à la victime de se sacrifier pour un enfant qu’elle n’a jamais choisi de concevoir.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The woman is innocent of the rape, pregnancy can intensify trauma, and simplistic slogans can compound her suffering.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La femme est innocente du viol, la grossesse peut intensifier le traumatisme et des slogans simplistes peuvent aggraver sa souffrance.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But isn’t compelling pregnancy itself a further violation of her body?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais imposer la poursuite de la grossesse n’est-il pas une nouvelle violation de son corps ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Original ACOG clinical FAQ/guideline was not independently collated in this pass
cases.scope_limitation: ACOG outlines ectopic options, not Catholic moral permissibility. Distinguish clinical urgency from disagreement about moral objects of individual procedures.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: If pregnancy will probably kill the mother, refusing abortion seems to prefer the fetus over the woman and may result in two deaths instead of one.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Si la grossesse risque probablement de tuer la mère, refuser l’avortement semble préférer le fœtus à la femme et peut conduire à deux morts au lieu d’une.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The dilemma can be medically terrifying. Catholic ethics must not answer it by pretending maternal life is less valuable or that doctors should do nothing.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le dilemme peut être médicalement terrifiant. La morale catholique ne doit pas y répondre en prétendant que la vie maternelle vaut moins ou que les médecins devraient ne rien faire.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Isn’t this just wordplay when everyone knows the fetus will die?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: N’est-ce pas un jeu de mots lorsque tout le monde sait que le fœtus mourra ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Francis to Spadaro 2013 interview, passage beginning 'We cannot insist only'
cases.scope_limitation: Francis explicitly objects to disproportionate pastoral insistence on only a few disputed moral topics while saying church teaching is clear. Original statement is a pastoral balance issue, not proof that sexual moral norms were revoked.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: In a 2013 interview with Antonio Spadaro, Pope Francis warned against insisting only on abortion, same-sex marriage and contraception and urged pastoral context. Why does sexual morality sometimes overshadow mercy, justice, economic wrongdoing and the rest of Christian discipleship?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dans son entretien de 2013 avec Antonio Spadaro, le pape François avertissait qu'il ne faut pas insister seulement sur l'avortement, le mariage homosexuel et la contraception et demandait de considérer le contexte pastoral. Pourquoi la morale sexuelle éclipse-t-elle parfois la miséricorde, la justice, les fautes économiques et l'ensemble de la vie chrétienne ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The criticism is sometimes deserved. A distorted religious culture can reduce moral formation to sexual prohibitions and neglect justice, charity, truthfulness, greed or cruelty.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La critique est parfois méritée. Une culture religieuse déformée peut réduire la formation morale aux interdictions sexuelles et négliger justice, charité, véracité, avidité ou cruauté.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Why do some Christian communities seem to emphasize sexual sins more than injustice, dishonesty, neglect of the poor or failures of charity?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Pourquoi certaines communautés chrétiennes semblent-elles insister davantage sur les péchés sexuels que sur l’injustice, la malhonnêteté, l’abandon des pauvres ou les manquements à la charité ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Freud original full text not independently accessible
cases.scope_limitation: Freud 1908 edition not retrievable; link to historical account is not current proof that traditional chastity causes neurosis.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Freud's 1908 essay connected restrictive sexual mores with nervous suffering and questioned whether everyone could redirect sexual desire without harm. Today, prolonged singleness, loneliness and omnipresent explicit media raise a related objection: can a demanding Catholic ethic of chastity be lived without damaging psychological wellbeing?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Dans son essai de 1908, Freud reliait certaines normes sexuelles restrictives à la souffrance nerveuse et doutait que chacun puisse détourner sans dommage son désir sexuel. Aujourd'hui, le célibat prolongé, la solitude et l'omniprésence des contenus explicites nourrissent une objection voisine : peut-on vivre une chasteté catholique exigeante sans nuire à l'équilibre psychologique ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The environment has changed in ways that genuinely increase exposure, temptation and the duration of unmarried adult life.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: L’environnement a changé d’une manière qui augmente réellement l’exposition, la tentation et la durée de la vie adulte non mariée.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But repeated failure seems to prove the standard is beyond many people.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais les échecs répétés semblent prouver que la norme dépasse beaucoup de personnes.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Empirical research links registered without full methods verification
cases.scope_limitation: 2026 purity/shame original research and survivor article were not read here; no causal clinical result should be inferred merely from titles.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Research and testimony describe some associations between restrictive religious sexual messages, shame and distress. This should be investigated seriously, but a reported association is not proof that every traditional norm causes the distress or that all religious formation is harmful.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Des études et des témoignages décrivent parfois une association entre messages religieux sexuels restrictifs, honte et détresse. Cela mérite une étude sérieuse, mais une association rapportée ne prouve ni que toute norme traditionnelle cause cette souffrance ni que toute formation religieuse soit nuisible.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Religious shame can be real, and humiliating or obsessive instruction can cause genuine harm.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: La honte religieuse peut être réelle, et un enseignement humiliant ou obsessionnel peut causer un véritable dommage.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: But if the same teaching repeatedly generates shame across many communities, doesn’t that implicate the doctrine itself?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Mais si le même enseignement génère régulièrement de la honte dans de nombreuses communautés, cela n’implique-t-il pas la doctrine elle-même ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: Fletcher original 1966 source not full-text accessible; excerpt sites secondary
cases.scope_limitation: 'Love is love' is a general slogan, not attributed to Fletcher as a direct quote. Original Fletcher Situation Ethics book limited to catalogue; synthetic case remains unattributed.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: 'Love is love' expresses a serious appeal to equal human dignity, affection and commitment. If partners are sincerely devoted to each other's good, why should a moral tradition deny that their sexual relationship is good?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: « L'amour, c'est l'amour » exprime un appel sérieux à l'égale dignité humaine, à l'affection et à l'engagement. Si deux partenaires recherchent sincèrement le bien l'un de l'autre, pourquoi une tradition morale refuserait-elle de juger bonne leur relation sexuelle ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Opponent proposition with precisely qualified authorship

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: The slogan expresses an important truth: affection, loyalty, sacrifice and personal dignity matter, and relationships should not be dismissed with contempt.
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Le slogan exprime une vérité importante : affection, loyauté, sacrifice et dignité personnelle comptent, et les relations ne doivent pas être rejetées avec mépris.
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Why this position may appeal, not an independent empirical proof

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Who gets to define the “true good” of the beloved rather than the couple themselves?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Qui peut définir le « vrai bien » de l’être aimé plutôt que le couple lui-même ?
reviewed_opponent_fields.source_role: Follow-up objection, often constructed, not a direct source quotation

cases.original_section_locator: APA 2008 original FAQ; independent ASRM original needed
cases.scope_limitation: APA's 2008 original orientation FAQ was read; ASRM fertility informed consent and other professional sources not independently collated, and no clinical findings alone adjudicate full sexual ethics.

reviewed_opponent_fields.live_english_text: Psychological and medical research can overturn factual assumptions about sexuality, distress and treatment outcomes. Professional bodies such as the APA and ASRM also defend access to services they regard as clinically appropriate. If Catholic moral conclusions rely partly on empirical premises that change, must those conclusions be reconsidered as well?
reviewed_opponent_fields.live_french_text: Les recherches psychologiques et médicales peuvent démentir certaines prémisses factuelles sur la sexualité, la souffrance et les effets des traitements. Des organismes comme l'APA et l'ASRM défendent aussi l'accès à des soins qu'ils jugent appropriés.
